profile.entities: GHCL Textiles Ltd — demerged from GHCL Ltd; standalone listed textiles arm
profile.mgmt: R.S. Jalan (Non-Exec Director); Raman Chopra (Non-Exec Director); Marshal Sonavane (CEO); M. Parasuraman (CFO); Manu Jain (Sr. GM Finance)
profile.subseg: Cotton/blended (synthetic) yarn; knitted & woven (greige) fabric; value-added / ready-to-cut & processed fabric; exports (Europe, Bangladesh, indirect US)
profile.themes: China+1 / FTA-driven export reorientation (US tariff resolution, India-EU FTA, UK/NZ FTAs); value-added vertical integration toward ready-to-cut fabric; PM MITRA Park (Virudhunagar, TN)

bull_bear.body:
- Net debt ₹118 cr, 0.1x net debt/equity — under-levered (analysts flagged ROE drag).
- **No buyback** despite eased regulations; cash to be deployed into growth capex (vertical integration).
- Dividend policy: 8–12% payout; FY26 payout retained at 8% (FY25 also 8%); ~30% dividend rate (vs 25%). 3 priorities: growth capex, shareholder reward, debt. Surplus beyond capex would lift payout.
- Non-core land parcel monetized (~₹8 cr profit).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Cotton:** Rising prices (₹55k→₹62k/candy); pre-buy bet on continued rise; ~30% import exposure + 11% duty + rupee depreciation (₹90→~96/USD) raise imported cotton & spares cost.
- **Demand / pass-through:** Big risk = whether downstream (fabric/garment) can absorb higher spreads amid inflation; China demand already tapering since March; Europe muted.
- **Spread sustainability:** ₹148/kg visible only through Q1 FY27; beyond depends on West Asia (US-Iran) conflict, fuel/gas, geopolitics.
- **Macro:** US-Iran conflict disrupting trade routes (shipment delays, logistics cost); volatile energy markets.
- **Working capital / ROE:** Elevated WC (~135–140 days; mgmt target 110–120); receivables +43% (revenue growth + earlier loose payment discipline). OCF down YoY (inventory + receivables).
- **Margin gap vs peers:** Ambika Cotton ~35% EBITDA vs GHCL ~30% (per analyst framing) — GHCL early in vertical-integration journey.
bull_bear.title: Risks

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic. Confident on near-term spreads (Q1) and structural FTA/China+1 tailwinds; candid about pass-through risk, China tapering, fuel/geopolitics, and being early in vertical-integration vs peers. R.S. Jalan closing: visibility of optimism returning after long headwind; on track for FY29–30 ₹2,000 cr + 15–18% EBITDA + double-digit ROCE.
bull_bear.title: Mgmt tone

bull_bear.body:
- Q4 yarn VOLUME actually dipped QoQ (~10,800→~10,400 tons); EBITDA growth was spread-driven, not volume-driven — analyst pushed on gross-margin vs spread mismatch (answer: unitized vs absolute, volume slightly lower).
- US exposure is INDIRECT (via fabric manufacturers), not direct — tariff resolution still mattered for demand.
- China bought Indian yarn in Q4 due to low Indian yarn prices + Chinese cotton acreage cut — a transient, now tapering tailwind.
- No inventory gains booked despite cotton rise; the ~₹8 cr land-sale gain is the real one-off boosting reported PAT.
- "Doubling revenue" in PPT = from original ~₹1,000 cr base to ~₹2,000 cr (NOT doubling current ₹1,335 cr to ₹2,600 cr) — mgmt clarified.
- ROCE only now becoming an explicit management KPI (improved ~1% this year; target double-digit).
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious points

bull_bear.body:
- "Strong balance sheet supports sustainable growth" is the only balance-sheet framing offered; the deck does not discuss dividends, buybacks or leverage.
- Reinvestment is channelled through the Rs. 1,035 Cr Tamil Nadu MoU programme, of which ~Rs. 675 Cr is already invested.
- Return focus: "Our focus remains on operational discipline, cost efficiency and working capital optimization, with scale and vertical integration expected to drive higher RoCE and sustainable growth", echoed as "scale, mix and integration upside supporting RoCE".
- Disclosed one-off: "FY26 Financials include one time gain of Rs. 8.59 Cr. on account of sale of non-strategic land."
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- Q4 strong on both volume AND pricing; knitting and weaving both improved; domestic demand improved meaningfully.
- Demand triggers: (a) resolution of US reciprocal/penalty tariffs (India sells to US indirectly via fabric makers) unleashed demand; (b) India-EU FTA → European inquiries concretized; (c) China yarn demand spike in Q4 (low Indian yarn prices + Chinese cotton acreage cut) — now tapering since March; (d) steady domestic QoQ/YoY growth.
- Exports ~14% of Q4 top line (up QoQ). Europe muted ~1–1.5 yrs but steady; Bangladesh strong; US only indirect (via fabric manufacturers).
- FTAs (UK/EU) not yet executed but supply chains reorienting to India; UK/EU customers placing trial orders.
business.title: Demand

business.body:
- **Yarn mix:** ~65–70% 100% cotton yarn; ~30–35% synthetic/blended (polyester-rich, cotton-rich, cellulosic blends).
- **Customer mix:** ~40–50% volume to concentrated strategic large brands; ~20–25% to brands via intermediaries/traders (direct brand communication); rest ~20–25% small/medium customers servicing brands.
- **Fabric:** ~12% of FY26 revenue (from 8%); targeting ~15% FY27, 16–18% once 40 machines installed. ~50% of fabric = knitted (in-house); woven stays outsourced. ~15–16 tons/day knitted (~12% of volume). Plan: 40% of yarn sold as yarn, 60% vertically integrated into fabric/processed fabric.
business.title: Segment (yarn / fabric)

business.body:
- China+1 / FTA reorientation (US tariff resolution, India-EU/UK FTAs) → Indian cotton/blended yarn & fabric exporters (GHCL via fabric makers + direct EU/Bangladesh). ⭐
- India cotton structural advantage (2nd-largest producer, low yield = production upside, spinning tech upgrade) → Indian cotton spinners vs global synthetic shift. ✅
- PM MITRA Park infrastructure → integrated textile players co-locating spinning + processing + ready-to-cut. ⭐

---
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries

business.body:
- Journey started with acquisition of a sick spinning unit in 2002, turned around to "one of the most reputed mills"; the spinning business was demerged to form GHCL Textiles Ltd effective April 1, 2023 (before demerger it was part of GHCL Limited).
- Two state-of-the-art manufacturing units with cutting-edge textile machinery, both located in Tamil Nadu, producing "high-quality tailor-made yarns, catering to domestic and international markets".
- Describes itself as a "Preferred supplier to premium customers both at domestic and international level with varied portfolio offerings", with "10+ Years Long Standing Relationship with Several Key Customers".
- Credibility framed through certifications (GRS, GIZA, CmiA), certified membership of the USTERIZED brand ("a symbol of excellence in spinning"), and a traceability platform for premium products covering source locations and environmental/social impact.
- Governance angle: "New independent directors and revamped management team is well positioned to strengthen corporate governance practices and drive the growth for GHCL Textiles."
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [India-UK CETA] The UK FTA "Commenced on 15th July" and removes a ~8-12% tariff disadvantage; the deck's tariff table shows Yarn & Fabrics and Garments moving from a pre-FTA 8-12% to a post-FTA 0%.
- [UK opportunity] Deck cites India's textile & apparel exports to the UK at US$1.9 Bn currently rising to US$3.5-4.0 Bn in 3-5 years, an "Incremental Opportunity US$ 1.5 - 2.0 Bn", with "Large headroom for growth as India's share in a ~US$30Bn UK market has been low".
- [FTA pipeline] Oman came into effect 3rd June with 5-10% duty removed for yarn, fabric & garment; New Zealand agreed (3-5% to 0% on yarn/fabric, ~10% to 0% for garments, ~8-10% landed-cost reduction); EU FTA agreed and implementing in 2027 (0% vs earlier ~8-12%); Canada (from 16-18%), Peru (10-16%), Israel (0-12%) and GCC (~5%) under negotiation.
- [US tariffs] "Tariffs reset ~10%" with "20%+ US cotton input = 0% duty on exports; vs 10% with Indian cotton. Mills can optimize per order."
- [Cotton policy & prices] "The 11% cotton import duty waived from 1st June is effective till 30th October 2026"; Indian cotton prices near global parity with a gap of ~0.5c/lb (79.5c vs 80.0c/lb), yarn-cotton spread expanded in Q1FY27, and acreage/output expected to rise next season.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body:
- **Cotton:** Prices rose ~₹55,000/candy (Dec '25) → ~₹62,000 currently. Mgmt pre-bought cotton ahead of rise → cost advantage expected as inventory flows through; ~120 days (~4 months) inventory as of 31-Mar; ~25–30% imported cotton, rest domestic. 11% import duty reinstated from January.
- **Power:** 3MW rooftop solar (~₹2 cr/yr full benefit); 10MW on-ground solar commissioning Jul–Aug FY27 (~₹6.5–7 cr full-yr, ~₹4.5 cr in FY27 partial as summer passes).
- **Energy/fuel:** Higher fuel prices pressuring synthetic portfolio + fabric manufacturing cost economics. Mgmt does NOT use gas in processes (no direct gas-availability hit), but value chain inflation a risk.
- EBITDA margin lifted to ~11.7% (Q4); R.S. Jalan: EBITDA up ~29% QoQ even ex one-time income, matching the ₹123→₹148 spread move.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost

latest_quarter.body: - **Q4 FY26 (this call):** Spread ₹148/kg (Q3 ₹123/kg); spread to continue into Q1 FY27. Rev ₹375 cr (+31% YoY); FY ₹1,335 cr (+14%); FY EBITDA ₹156 cr (+34%). Yarn vol ~10,400 t (down from ~10,800 Q3). Net debt ₹118 cr (0.1x). Cotton ₹55k→₹62k/candy; 120-day cotton inventory pre-bought. Fabric 12% of rev (from 8%), target 15% FY27 / 16–18% post-40 machines. New 25k spindles stabilized (98%+ util); 40 knitting machines in build (15 in, +25 from Q3 FY27). PM MITRA Park ~50 acres allotted. One-off: ~₹8 cr land-sale gain; NO inventory gain. FY27 capex ₹100–120 cr; ~₹350 cr pending (fabric/processing). Dividend payout 8% retained. Guidance anchor: ₹2,000 cr rev + 15–18% EBITDA by FY29–30; double-digit ROCE goal. No buyback.
latest_quarter.title: QoQ Log

outlook.body:
- **Volume:** No exact volume guidance. FY27 volume uplift mainly from full-year run of new 25,000 spindles (operated only ~2 quarters in FY26), plus 40 knitting machines (15 installed, +25 from Q3 FY27, ~60% landing Q2–Q3). Mgmt: growth "not only from volume" — also product mix/price maximization. New 25k spindle peak quarterly rev ~₹50–60 cr spinning (₹250–300 cr/yr incl. knitting); currently at ~70–75% contribution.
- **Spread:** Q4 spread of **₹148/kg expected to CONTINUE into Q1 FY27** with high visibility ("conservatively certain"); could go up. Beyond Q1 depends on geopolitics/fuel. China yarn demand tapering since March.
- **Capex:** FY27 capex **₹100–120 cr** — ₹35 cr on-ground 10MW solar; ₹15 cr knitting machines; balance PM MITRA Park land + replacement/infra capex. Remaining ~₹300–350 cr (of original ₹1,000 cr plan; ~₹675 cr already deployed) over next 3 yrs, mostly toward **fabric + processing** (ready-to-cut). Asset turn on incremental fabric/processing ~1.5x.
- **Margin:** Normal EBITDA ~15% (10-yr track); targeting **15–18% EBITDA margin** over next 3 yrs via vertical integration + premium product mix + 98–99% utilization. FY27 growth expected "near about" FY26 level (±2% delta).
- **Long-term anchor:** ~**₹2,000 cr revenue** + 15–18% EBITDA by **FY29–FY30** (revenue ~FY29, margin ~FY30). ROCE focus added — aiming for double-digit ROCE (improved ~1% this year).
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL)

outlook.body:
- **PM MITRA Park (Virudhunagar, TN):** ~50-acre land allotment received — strategic; to host processing + ready-to-cut fabric; "next phase of scale growth and product integration." Details TBD.
- **Vertical integration → ready-to-cut fabric supplier** is the core vision; ~₹350 cr pending capex skewed to fabric/processing (higher asset turn ~1.5x) to bridge to ₹2,000 cr.
- New 25,000-spindle unit stabilized at optimum utilization; knitting machine expansion underway.
- Rooftop + on-ground solar (energy cost optionality). FY27 = first full year of new capacity benefit.
outlook.title: Growth / optionality

deepdive.thesis: A spinning-heavy yarn player de-risking via vertical integration into knitted/processed "ready-to-cut" fabric, riding an FY26 spread upcycle (₹123→₹148/kg) and FTA/China+1 export tailwinds, with a multi-year ₹2,000 cr revenue + 15–18% EBITDA goal anchored on PM MITRA Park capex by FY29–30.
